raw_text:
The research aims to uncover why sites employing the same nominal work process experience varying completion times and identify the quantifiable factors contributing to these differences. It seeks to differentiate between potential explanations through careful observation and analysis.

Assumptions
It is assumed that measurable factors lie at the heart of the observed completion-time discrepancies across sites, despite identical nominal work processes.

Research design
This study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data analysis with qualitative observations. First, site-level completion times will be collected and statistically analyzed to identify patterns and differences. Second, direct observations and interviews will be conducted at each site to explore contextual and situational factors influencing performance.

Data or evidence needed
- Completion time records from each site for a predefined period.
- Observational field notes of operational practices and environments.
- Interview transcripts discussing site-specific procedures and challenges.

Measurement
- Completion time: The duration from the start of a work process to its completion.
- Quantitative metrics on resources allocated and utilization levels.
- Observational checks on adherence to standard procedures.
- Interview structured to probe practices and bottlenecks.

Analysis
The quantitative data will undergo statistical analysis to pinpoint significant predictors of completion time. Any identified variables will then be validated through the qualitative observations and interviews, which will also help explore attitudes and motivations influencing observed behaviors.

Decision/ Stopping rule
The research will conclude when identifying a robust set of measurable predictors along with a coherent explanation to account for the observed completion-time variations. Progress reassessments will occur quarterly to ensure data integrity and relevance.

Limitations
Limitations include potential biases in interviewee responses and challenges in generalizing findings from a limited sample size. Controlling for external variables influencing site performance, such as managerial decisions or technological disruptions, will be a key focus to refine the analysis.
